revision_rule.note: The map() array method and its result-shape and element-type guarantees are absent from IEEE 1800-2012.
The map() array method and its shape, index-type, and result-element-type guarantees are absent from IEEE 1800-2017.
The 2012 syntax permits only an optional iterator_argument; it does not provide the later optional index_argument.
IEEE 1800-2017 permits only an optional iterator_argument in the parenthesized method arguments; it does not provide the 2023 index_argument form.
The 2012 rule defines the element iterator and default item binding, but has no index_argument or default index querying-method binding.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines the explicit/default element iterator and its scope, but has no separate index_argument binding or default index name.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not specify the later implicit-variable use and postfix placement guarantee for array method calls.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define array method calls as implicit variables or specify postfix range-select/property placement around a with clause.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not state the later combined rule expressly permitting whole/element associative operations while prohibiting associative-array slices.
IEEE 1800-2017 states that slice read/write operations can be performed on all packed or unpacked arrays and does not state the 2023 associative-array exception.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define the later hard-packed versus soft-packed untagged union forms or soft qualifier.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no soft packed union construct or hard-versus-soft packed-union size rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no array-method iterator index() querying facility or dimension-numbering rule for it.
IEEE 1800-2012 fixes the iterator method name as index and provides no optional array-call index argument to rename it.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no iterator index-method name or optional array-method index argument.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines function index(int dimension=1) with a fixed method name, rather than the later customizable index_method_name.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no iterator index() method or its dimension-argument signature.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no iterator index() method and therefore no corresponding return-type or wildcard-array restriction.
IEEE 1800-2012 requires packed for a packed dimension on either struct or union and does not provide the later soft union alternative.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires packed for a packed dimension on either struct or union and has no soft qualifier alternative for unions.
IEEE 1800-2012 includes random_qualifier in struct_union_member grammar but does not state the later restriction limiting it to unpacked structures.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define soft packed unions or their recursive width and alignment representation.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no soft packed union construct or corresponding width, alignment, and recursive representation rules.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not define soft packed unions or the later narrow-member write preservation behavior.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no soft packed union construct or member-write MSB-preservation guarantee.
The 2012 struct_union grammar has no soft union qualifier and lacks the later random-qualifier restriction, so its permitted qualifier set differs.
IEEE 1800-2017 has the same aggregate-member framework but its struct_union grammar lacks the 2023 soft union qualifier.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not specify the later minimum support guarantee of 16777216 unpacked-array elements.
